newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zaire's Mobutu arrives in France, aid force mooted.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Mobutu arrives in France, aid force mooted.

text.p: Zaire's ailing president Mobutu Sese Seko arrived in the French Riviera capital of Nice from Switzerland on Monday and French diplomatic sources said he would head home to his troubled country in a few days.

An airport spokesman said the 66-year-old Zairean president, who has a luxury villa nearby and a permanent entry visa into France, flew in aboard his private jet as his country stumbled towards chaos.

French diplomatic sources said he would stay for a few days before heading home. There was no plan for him to meet French President Jacques Chirac who arrived on Monday in Marseille, about 200 km (120 miles) west of Nice, for a two-day Franco-Spanish summit.

Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes told reporters at the summit that Paris and Madrid were in favour of considering the creation of an international force to guarantee distribution of humanitarian aid in Zaire.
He said that creating the force would need the support of the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity.
Matutes said both Rwanda and Zaire would have to agree not to place obstacles in the way of distributing humanitarian aid.
"If these conditions exist, France and Spain are in favour of considering the creation of this force, for which the collaboration of the United States will also be very important," he said.
Fighting between rival groups in Zaire has forced about a million refugees onto the roads and France has called for international action to help save them from disaster.
Mobutu had been in Switzerland since August when he underwent surgery for prostate cancer at the University Hospital in Lausanne.
He arrived aboard a four-engined DC-8 aircraft specially designed for him and which can carry several dozen people, the airport spokesman said.

He made no statement on arrival and was whisked off to an undisclosed location presumed to be his sprawling personal residence at Roquebrune Cap-Martin, one of the choicest, most picturesque areas of the Riviera, just east of Monaco.
Officials in Paris said earlier they did not know Mobutu was arriving.

Mobutu, a one-time army sergeant who seized power in 1965, had been living with his entourage of more than 20 at Lausanne's luxury Beau-Rivage Palace hotel, but Swiss authorities were understood to have asked him to avoid public appearances or interviews.

A special United Nations envoy, Raymond Chretien, had been expecting to visit him in Lausanne this week to discuss fighting in eastern Zaire and the plight of a million mostly Hutu refugees from Rwanda and Burundi.
Swiss television reported last month that Mobutu's villa in the south of France was being prepared for use and he might continue his treatment there.
Last week former French internal affairs minister Charles Pasqua visited him in Lausanne.
Mobutu's arrival in France places him in the country which is emerging as champion of foreign intervention in Zaire.

French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette had earlier in the day urged the United States, European and African countries on Monday to hold urgent talks on how to restore security in eastern Zaire and help avert disaster for more than one million refugees fleeing fighting.
